title: Downhole Studio training
data: Synthetic example survey generated by Downhole Studio (32 depths, P and opposite-direction S shots, reference geophone with trigger jitter); no customer data.

segments.speech: Welcome to the Downhole Studio training video from Quake Logic. In the next few minutes you will take a downhole seismic survey from raw S E G two records to reviewed P and S picks, a layered velocity model, V s 30, and a finished report.

The first time Downhole Studio starts, it offers a fourteen day free trial, or activation with a licence key. Licensing sends only a hashed computer identifier. Your survey data never leaves your computer. When the trial is running, the start screen opens.

Click New Project. Give the survey a name and a job number. Everything you do from here on is kept in one project file, together with the original records, so another engineer can reproduce your analysis.

On the Import page, drag in the S E G two files, or add a whole folder. Every file is inspected before anything is imported. The checks list sample rates, channels, duplicates, and the depth sequence, as errors, warnings, or information. Nothing is repaired silently. When the preview looks right, click Import. The original files are stored byte for byte, with checksums.

On the Geometry page, enter the borehole details and the horizontal offsets of the P and S sources. The two sources have their own offsets, and the borehole diagram updates as you type. Then assign each record to a depth and a shot type, here by acquisition order: one P shot and two opposite S shots at every depth, from the top down.

Before processing, look at every trace. The waveform viewer shows all depths, raw or processed. Scroll to zoom in time, and click a trace to see its details in the inspector. The spectrum below shows the dominant frequency of the selected trace.

Processing never changes the recorded data. Each component has its own chain of steps, applied to a copy, and every step can be switched off, edited, or removed. For picking, keep processing light. Here a gentle band pass is added to the horizontal components, to make the shear waves easier to review.

A reference geophone at the source records the true moment of every hammer blow. Pick its onsets automatically, then choose a correction. Subtract reference onset measures every arrival from the moment the source was struck, which removes the trigger delay and the shot to shot jitter. The raw times are always kept.

On the P Picks page, run the automatic picker. The A I C picker is recommended. Every automatic pick gets a confidence score, and the inspector explains it: signal to noise ratio, onset sharpness, agreement between algorithms, and consistency with neighbouring depths.

Review every depth. Click to place a pick, drag it, or nudge it one sample at a time with the arrow keys. When you agree with the automatic picks, mark them reviewed. Manual picks are never overwritten by running the picker again.

Shear waves are picked on the horizontal components. Because the S source is struck at both ends, the shear wave reverses polarity between the two shots, while P energy and noise do not. Downhole Studio picks on the half difference of the two shots, and the depth detail overlays them, so you can confirm the shear arrival. If the probe rotated between depths, polarization analysis finds the best horizontal direction, but it is only applied when you choose.

The travel time graph shows the corrected arrivals against depth. Each straight segment is a layer, and its slope is one over the velocity. Click Suggest boundaries, review the suggestions, and apply the ones you agree with. You can drag any boundary, and everything updates immediately. Choose the method: layer regression, interval velocities, or refracted ray layer stripping, which follows Snell's law and is the most accurate near the surface.

The Engineering page computes Poisson's ratio and the shear, Young's, and bulk moduli for every layer. Density is never assumed. Enter measured values, one constant, or deliberately choose an empirical estimate, which is then labelled as estimated. V s 30 is calculated from measured data only, unless you explicitly allow extrapolation.

The Results page shows how trustworthy the analysis is. Every automatic check is explained in plain language, and clicking a finding takes you to the depth or layer concerned. The verdict is advisory. It does not certify compliance with any standard, and results always need professional review.

Finally, fill in the client, site, and company details on the Report page, choose the sections, and preview the report page by page. Generate P D F writes the finished report, with the methodology, quality control, figures, tables, and the full processing history. Tables export to Excel and C S V at full precision, and every figure exports as P N G, S V G, or P D F.
That is the complete workflow. The sample project on the start screen shows a finished survey, and the field guide explains how to record one. Thank you for choosing Downhole Studio from Quake Logic.
